ranked.headline: Spatial and single-cell models now separate technical noise from biological variation
ranked.summary: New preprints remove transcript spillover in imaging spatial data, attach confidence to histology-based expression inference and noise-correct benchmarks.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is spatial and single-cell modeling that explicitly separates technical artifact from biological signal. In imaging-based spatial transcriptomics, Dancer uses a reference-guided probabilistic framework to distinguish within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination. SYNDRI, a transformer trained on simulated data, removes transcript spillover. For histology-to-expression prediction, REGAIN attaches per-prediction confidence and reports gains in cell-type annotation and prognostic value in TCGA-BRCA. A noise-corrected correlation metric (RSC) is proposed for benchmarking such predictions. A second strand targets integration and imputation: scOnion scores cell-level RNA–chromatin concordance, scRefine applies hierarchical contrastive learning to atlas integration and rare-population annotation, BRIDGE performs contrastive cross-tissue imputation on GTEx, and GASTON-VI learns spatial axes across samples and modalities. Network and state-level analyses (CHO iModulons, CAR T gene-dependency spectra, UCE state bridges, lung adenocarcinoma Global Tumor Time) are adjacent. All are preprints, so reported gains remain unreviewed.

ranked.headline: Perturbation and drug-response models shift toward explicit noise, bias and uncertainty modeling
ranked.summary: Benchmarks and new models for CRISPRi, combinatorial and siRNA perturbation response now treat assay noise, label heterogeneity and graph bias as first-class terms.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is prediction of cellular and molecular responses to perturbation, with explicit statistical treatment of the noise and bias in the training labels. The Virtual Cell Challenge 2026 formalizes six metrics for zero-shot prediction of transcriptional responses to CRISPRi knockdowns, setting a shared evaluation target. GAIN predicts single-cell combinatorial perturbation responses by decomposing them into an additive baseline plus a learned non-additive interaction term. DeepCINET makes viability assay noise part of a ranking objective for cell line drug response, while siGMA uses a heteroscedastic multimodal formulation with calibrated uncertainty for chemically modified siRNA silencing efficacy across heterogeneous datasets. Related work corrects structural artifacts rather than label noise: Inverse Node Frequency normalizes metapath features to reduce hub bias in target-adverse event knowledge graphs. PTM-BDL and BrainRoute extend the theme to site-resolved phosphosite-aware drug response and community-verified BBB permeability.

ranked.headline: Pluripotent stem cell models scale up: vitreous, olfactory, heart organoids and ex utero embryos
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend PSC-derived models to new tissues (vitreous, olfactory epithelium) and benchmark fidelity across heart organoid protocols and cell systems.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the expansion and benchmarking of in vitro developmental models built from pluripotent or embryonic cells. New tissue targets appear. Centimeter-scale human vitreous organoids were derived via TGF-beta signaling and mirror human vitreous structure. Human iPSC-derived olfactory sensory organoids show neuronal and glial diversity, maturation signatures matching fetal nasal tissue, and network bursting. In embryology, mouse zygotes were cultured continuously ex utero to early organogenesis after BMP inhibition and culture optimization, forming axes and organ primordia. Fidelity assessment is a parallel theme. An integrated single-cell atlas of 16 heart organoid datasets benchmarks developmental fidelity across protocols. Transcriptomic aging readouts in iPSC-derived neurons were used to test eight candidate geroprotectors, with mTORC1 and MEK-ERK pathways identified as tunable. Two adjacent studies apply these platforms in other settings. One is a TSPAN10 knockout in hESC-derived RPE affecting pigmentation, polarity and antioxidant defence. The other profiles bovine MSCs across culture systems for cultivated meat.

ranked.headline: Spatial and single-cell atlases chart tissue remodeling across aging, disease and repair
ranked.summary: New preprints use scRNAseq and spatial transcriptomics to map state-dependent remodeling in liver, lung, adipose, mammary, cervical and gut tissue.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is single-cell and spatial transcriptomic mapping of how tissues reorganize across physiological, pathological and regenerative states. In human metabolic liver disease, senescent SenSpots localize to portal tracts and fibrotic septa, with phenotypes shifting during progression. Aging male mouse inguinal white adipose tissue contains lipid-associated macrophages with age-linked inflammatory and metabolic features. A rat post-pneumonectomy atlas combines scRNAseq, Xenium and NICHES connectomics across post-operative days to resolve compensatory lung regrowth. Saanen goat mammary tissue shows period-specific epithelial, stromal and immune remodeling between dry period and peak lactation. Two studies address baseline or environmental context rather than remodeling trajectories: snRNAseq of healthy human endocervix and ectocervix maps ten cell types and shows that sampling method affects epithelial recovery, and a mouse ileum survey compares germ-free, defined 12-strain and SPF microbiota for effects on host co-expression networks. What is new is spatially anchored resolution of niche-level cell states, including senescent, macrophage and luminal populations, across distinct tissue conditions.

ranked.headline: Toxic metabolite buildup countered by mTOR inhibition, mRNA enzyme delivery and thiol systems
ranked.summary: New preprints converge on relieving metabolite overload—BCAAs, cystine, long-chain acyl intermediates, ceramides, iron—through pharmacologic, genetic and redox routes.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the handling of metabolites that become cytotoxic when enzymatic or transport capacity is exceeded, and the interventions that restore flux. In maple syrup urine disease mice, the mTOR inhibitor rapamycin lowers branched-chain amino acid accumulation, reduces neuroinflammation and extends survival. Lipid nanoparticle delivery of both Hadha and Hadhb mRNA reconstitutes hepatic trifunctional protein and fatty acid oxidation in a mouse model, an enzyme-replacement counterpart to the pharmacologic approach. A parallel set addresses thiol and iron chemistry: TXNDC17 acts with glutathione to prevent cystine buildup and cystine-induced death, while the fungal anthraquinone bostrycin targets TXNRD1 and perturbs iron, redox and glutathione metabolism to drive ferroptosis. Lipid-side control appears in the DES1 inhibitor PR280, which raises ceramides broadly with limited specificity. Hepatocyte NDRG1 adds a post-translational layer, promoting GAMT-dependent creatine production that suppresses PHB1 succinylation during acetaminophen injury.

ranked.headline: Chromatin and DNA modification states shape neuronal gene regulation across aging, differentiation and disease variants
ranked.summary: Six preprints link histone marks, cytosine modifications and allelic chromatin to neuronal activation, differentiation and transcript regulation.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is epigenetic and regulatory-state control of gene expression, with most items centered on neural cells. In aged mouse dentate gyrus, an H3K9me3-high state formed via Suv39h1 blunts neuronal activation and synaptic remodeling, and reducing these neurons improves memory. During mouse ES cell neuronal differentiation, single-base profiling reveals a 5hmC-to-5mC transition at gene bodies and transcription end sites. In human iPSC neurogenesis, H19 isoform switching separates a pluripotency-associated non-canonical variant from canonical H19 and IGF2 expression. In human microglia, allele-specific open chromatin ties the AUD-associated variant rs7307261 to altered ETS-factor binding. TrES-seq adds joint scRNA and histone-mark profiling in human tonsil cells, and a cross-species adipose study addresses transposable elements in aging, extending the theme beyond neurons.

ranked.headline: Deleterious and standing variation shape selection, genetic load, and breeding and conservation outcomes
ranked.summary: New simulations and a review link deleterious and standing variation to genetic load, climate adaptation limits, gene drive outcomes, and crop breeding.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how the distribution of fitness-relevant variation, including deleterious alleles, constrains evolutionary and applied outcomes. A review covers identification, cross-species variation, and persistence of deleterious mutations, with implications for crop breeding and conservation. Forward simulations indicate that reproductive competition amplifies purifying selection and reduces genetic load more efficiently than the comparison scenario. Individual-based mosquito models show that standing genetic variation evolves in response to a homing suppression drive and alters drive conversion and resistance outcomes. In Boechera stricta, genome-environment analyses identify climate-linked SNPs, suggesting that hot, dry projected climates may exceed adaptive capacity. In admixed crop germplasm, simulations show that low founder isoeliteness reduces genomic selection gain, which an isoeliteness-guided method addresses. Most evidence here is simulation-based or preprint-stage.

ranked.headline: Tubulin and spindle disruption in progenitors drives cortical malformation in TTC5 and dynein models
ranked.summary: Two TTC5 studies and a dynein organoid study converge on mitotic and tubulin defects in cortical progenitors, alongside p53-dependent mesenchymal defects in a DBA model.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is disease-variant models that trace developmental malformation to progenitor-level cytoskeletal and mitotic defects. Ttc5 knockout mice show brain malformations from neurogenesis defects and mitotic errors with elevated γ-tubulin, extending tubulin autoregulation to TTC5. A mouse model of a patient TTC5 nonsense mutation reports impaired progenitor expansion, mitosis, tubulin homeostasis and neuronal arborization. Patient-derived cortical organoids with dynein variants show spindle disorganization and apoptosis, with differing impact across variants. Two items address related but distinct questions: RPS19 haploinsufficiency in mesenchymal progenitors causes p53-dependent growth plate defects independent of hematopoietic failure in a Diamond Blackfan anemia model, and Capsaspora shows a Hippo-dystrophin axis maintaining cortical actin. New here is the independent, convergent TTC5 evidence linking tubulin homeostasis to cortical development, and the variant-specific dynein organoid comparison.

ranked.headline: Regulatory elements and progenitor programs define human-specific timing in cortical development
ranked.summary: Six preprints resolve enhancers, transposable elements, progenitor regulators and neurogenic lineages in developing human cortex, plus a visualization tool.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the regulatory logic of human cortical development at single-cell and cross-species resolution. Locus-resolved long-read profiling in organoids implicates human-specific transposable elements in the timing of the radial glia-to-neuron transition. Cross-species multiomics identifies RHOJ as an oRG-enriched regulator of human-enriched progenitor states. A single-nucleus accessibility atlas of 1.17M candidate enhancers across 104k mid-gestation nuclei supplies a lineage-restricted regulatory reference. Two further preprints address downstream organization: expression timing predicts dosage dominance, tracking neuronal-glial fate, and direct versus indirect neurogenesis yields transcriptomically distinct extratelencephalic neurons with functional differences in motor cortex. VEGABrain is a visualization resource that maps bulk RNA-seq and ssGSEA enrichment onto brain atlas surfaces, not an experimental finding.

ranked.headline: Reference choice and genome structure shape variant, expression and trait interpretation in plants
ranked.summary: Preprints link graph pangenomes, mapping strategy and TE insertions to trait and expression interpretation across plant and fungal genomes.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that interpretation of genotype, expression and trait data depends on the quality and structure of the reference. In Capsicum, a graph pangenome anchors k-mer GWAS signals for pungency and aroma terpene traits to Pun1 haplotypes and TPS genes. A six-species comparison of TopHat2, HISAT2 and STAR reports genome-guided mapping errors for tandemly duplicated genes. In six bread wheat cultivars, cultivar-specific TE insertions in gene bodies track homoeolog expression bias, mainly through suppression. The Rhizoctonia solani AG1-IB assembly resolves haplotypes of a heterokaryotic pathogen, with ~97.75% identity between them. Tipularia discolor shows candidate gene mining on a fragmented assembly, and MEAM-OWL adds browser-based motif enrichment tied to expression. New here is the use of pangenome and haplotype-resolved frameworks to localize variation.

ranked.headline: Noncoding risk variants are resolved to effector genes via splicing, transcript usage, SVs and perturbation
ranked.summary: Six preprints extend variant-to-gene mapping beyond expression eQTLs to splicing, structural variants, and single-variant perturbation in disease tissues.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is assigning disease-associated noncoding variants to effector genes within relevant tissue or cell contexts, with several studies looking beyond total gene abundance. In IBD colon samples (1,149), joint eQTL and sQTL mapping identifies colocalized expression and splicing effects, implicating NMD and immune pathways. For type 2 diabetes, 338 fine-mapped signals are colocalized with adipose expression, splicing and transcript usage, and CELL-X uses islet single-cell data to prioritize beta cells and genes such as SLC30A8 and TCF7L2. Pangenome genotyping in CARTaGENE adds 103 SV-eQTLs. MPRA and CRISPR perturbation in chondrocytes link rs1895062 to PAPPA in osteoarthritis. The IGVF Catalog integrates 657 datasets as supporting infrastructure.

ranked.headline: Methods separate cell-type identity and composition from within-cell regulatory variation in bulk and single-cell data
ranked.summary: Six preprints apply statistical and sequence-based models to resolve cell types, composition and regulatory links from methylation, chromatin and multiome data.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is attributing signal to specific cell types or states rather than to bulk averages or shared confounders. EPIC2 links GWAS summary statistics with single-cell chromatin accessibility to identify trait-relevant cell types. LongReadClock builds cell-type-resolved epigenetic clocks from bulk blood long-read methylation, separating composition effects. CREMAP adjusts latent shared technical and biological variation before testing peak-gene links in single-cell multiome data. EMBHER shows Borzoi sequence-to-function embeddings capture whole-blood expression heritability. A CHIP multi-omic study of 466 samples reports distinct effects across driver genes, and Pooch uses differentially methylated CpGs to assign parent of origin in Hi-C-phased assemblies. New here is the use of long-read methylation for cell-type-resolved ageing; all results are preprint-level.

ranked.headline: Plasma cfDNA and genome-wide InDel taxonomy extend detection of somatic mutational processes
ranked.summary: New preprints detect tissue-derived somatic mutations and clonal mosaicism from plasma, and refine InDel signatures in 887 myeloma genomes.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is measuring somatic change in tissue without direct sampling or at finer mutational resolution. Two cfDNA preprints report that ultra-sensitive plasma sequencing detects clonal mosaicism and liver-derived somatic mutations in chronic liver disease, with ulcerative colitis also covered for mosaicism; the liver study reports etiology-linked patterns and a reduction after intervention. A refined InDel taxonomy applied to 887 multiple myeloma whole genomes broadens the repertoire of mutational processes, identifies a TXNDC5 hotspot, and links signatures to treatment outcome. A benchmark of sample mispairing detection tools in multimodal cancer datasets addresses sample-identity quality control rather than mutagenesis. FiberTron and the TNBC Perturb-seq network study concern regulatory variant effects and gene regulatory inference, adjacent to the mutational theme.

ranked.headline: Representation probing and structured models test what biological deep networks encode
ranked.summary: Six preprints test what biological foundation models encode and whether simpler or structured designs match them, using annotations, perturbations and encoders.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is scrutiny of what learned biological representations contain, rather than accuracy alone. Sparse autoencoder features from transcriptomic foundation models largely behave as gene detectors on spatial panels, and interpretability conclusions for ESMC protein language models depend on residue-level curated annotations. A 4-D value track and simple encodings retain most performance in single-cell foundation models, questioning 512-dimensional value embeddings. Other work builds structure in: CIRCE uses a Boltzmann distribution over Hamming distance in combinatorial perturbation space to infer input identity and graded signaling strength, and CMC-VAE links genes and proteins causally in CITE-seq data, with interventions refining perturbation predictions. SimpleP2G compares image encoders for predicting expression from pathology images, favoring Virchow2 features with a simple frozen-embedding decoder.

ranked.headline: Clock, transcriptional and m6A layers set timing and magnitude of plant temperature and drought responses
ranked.summary: New work resolves how clock factors and RNA regulation time heat, autumn warming, drought and cold-linked ripening responses in Arabidopsis, potato, spruce, wheat and peach.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is regulatory control of response timing and output under environmental stress. In Arabidopsis, CCA1 and LHY mutants alter time-of-day heat responses across transcriptome, proteome and metabolome, implicating sulfur and ROS processes. In cultivated potato, diel expression phase differs from wild Solanum species independently of clock period, with DOF and REVEILLE transcription factors linked to the shifts. In white spruce, autumn warming decouples photosynthesis and cold-acclimation gene networks from growth cessation, with MYB and AP2/ERF regulators implicated. Two Plant Physiology studies add post-transcriptional control: m6A and metabolomic profiling in wheat drought tolerance, and the cold-repressed demethylase PpALKBH9 stabilizing PpFUL4 mRNA to promote ethylene-associated ripening in peach. Relative to earlier emphasis, the focus is now on phase shifts, decoupling of programs and epitranscriptomic regulation.

ranked.headline: Resolution limits of marker-gene and short-read microbiome profiling are being addressed
ranked.summary: New tools and surveys expose and correct blind spots in microbiome profiling, from missed sludge taxa to eukaryotic bycatch, while host identity structures communities.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how method choice shapes microbial community interpretation. HiFi long-read metagenomics shows that short-read assemblies of activated sludge miss denitrifiers, nitrifiers and Accumulibacter, biasing N2O-related inferences. RADSuite adds RADlib, a curated 16S rRNA gene copy database, and RADx, which identifies V regions to enable species-level identification. metaEukaryome uses mitochondrial and plastid sequences to detect eukaryotes in 75,727 global metagenomes, revealing cross-domain co-occurrence. Host-associated 16S surveys apply marker-gene profiling: octocoral microbiomes in Florida are stable over three years, driven by host identity and host-specific Endozoicomonas, while Antarctic Haliclystus antarcticus communities vary across gut, peduncle and tentacles, with an antimicrobial gut Oceanisphaera ostreae isolate. The new element is the focus on correcting resolution and taxonomic-scope biases in profiling.

ranked.headline: Phosphorylation and phase separation remodel ER-membrane contacts and the cortex
ranked.summary: New work resolves how E-Syt2 and Pil1 phosphorylation and FRM condensates reorganize ER-plasma membrane interfaces, alongside cytoskeletal patterning cues.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is regulated organization of the cell cortex and ER-plasma membrane interfaces. In mitosis, phosphorylation of E-Syt2 drives loss of ERPM contact sites, and retaining them delays cell progression. In fission yeast, Pdk1 phosphorylates Pil1 to disassemble eisosomes and remodel plasma membrane and cortical ER at the division site, enabling Mid1 recruitment. Complementary preprints show that FRM-4 and FRM-1 phase separation partitions ER-plasma membrane junctions into calcium-release and calcium-reentry subdomains, and that a specialized extracellular matrix patterns the microtubule regulator EFA-6 at neuron-epidermis interfaces. The MTCL1/2 study extends the cytoskeletal theme to the Golgi region, where katanin and CAPZ recruitment coordinates microtubules and actin for secretory vesicle docking. New here is the mechanistic resolution of phosphorylation and condensate-based control at membrane contacts and cortex.

ranked.headline: Models link movement, plasticity and trade-offs to coexistence and evolutionary outcomes
ranked.summary: New models tie herbivore movement, plasticity, viral traits, cross-feeding and host mobility to coexistence, diversity and virulence evolution.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is that interaction structure, spatial or trophic, determines how individual-level traits scale to population, coexistence and evolutionary outcomes. A spatially explicit individual-based model couples herbivore movement and landscape structure to resource depletion and population dynamics. A parasite model shows that impaired host mobility favours reduced virulence through altered relatedness and host density. Coexistence theory is extended to competition-induced plasticity, which alters niche and fitness differences, and viral maturation and lysis plasticity is linked to nutrient inflow and host availability. A bacteria-yeast model finds that an excretion-reliance trade-off governs coexistence, biodiversity and collapse risk. What is new is the explicit pairing of trait plasticity or trade-offs with evolutionary and demographic responses. All items are model-based, so conclusions depend on model assumptions.

ranked.headline: Automated home-cage and vocal readouts quantify social behavior in mouse models
ranked.summary: Five preprints apply automated tracking, information theory, LLM interfaces and vocalization analysis to social and communicative phenotypes in mice.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is automated, quantitative phenotyping of social and communicative behavior in mice. LMT-MCP links the Live Mouse Tracker database to LLMs for natural-language behavioral analysis, while an RFID home-cage approach uses mutual information on positional data to quantify social dependence, validated against three-chamber sociability. Applied to genetic models, Shank3 knockouts show heightened engagement with familiar cagemates but altered, more antagonistic behavior toward strangers. Two preprints address neonatal ultrasonic vocalizations: one analyzes about 59,000 pup calls across postnatal days 0-5, finding age- and context-dependent call-type shifts, and Foxg1 models show opposing call-duration effects that depend on the mutation. The items emphasize scalable readouts and developmental or context dependence rather than a shared 3D pose method.

ranked.headline: Open tools quantify and infer cell states from morphology, spatial context and multimodal data
ranked.summary: Five preprints release open tools for microglial morphology, single-cell exploration, connectomics and spatial inference of cell-state transitions.
ranked.synthesis: The items share an emphasis on accessible computational tools for resolving cell state and cellular context, with only one addressing microglia directly. PolyMorph3D, an open-source MATLAB tool, quantifies 3D microglia morphology and colocalization with up to four markers in mouse and human tissue. Niche-FATE applies optimal transport that combines expression, spatial neighbourhoods and ligand-receptor signalling to infer cell-state transitions from spatiotemporal data. A kidney spatial transcriptomics study infers networks of interacting subcellular processes across cellular neighborhoods. SingloCell (multimodal single-cell exploration) and Jump (EM connectomics annotation) lower access barriers to large datasets. What is new is the pairing of morphological or spatial-niche readouts with open, browser- or code-based analysis, rather than new biological findings on microglia or macrophage state dynamics.

ranked.headline: Glial lysosomal and metabolic programs track neurodegeneration in mouse models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints resolve cell-type-specific glial, metabolic and hypothalamic responses to amyloid and frontotemporal pathology.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is cell-type-resolved glial and metabolic responses accompanying amyloid and frontotemporal pathology. Two preprints place lysosomal programs at the centre of microglial reprogramming. A MiT/TFE lysosomal biogenesis program precedes and couples to disease-associated microglia (DAM) reprogramming across murine injury, amyloidosis and human AD. A GPNMB-marked, TREM2-dependent lysosomal state in FTD/AD mice is reversible and tracks neurodegeneration severity along the DAM continuum. Metabolic readouts extend this to astrocytes: human posterior cingulate proteomics and transcriptomics, combined with MRS and hyperpolarized pyruvate imaging in APP-KI mice, implicate glia in mitochondrial alterations. Single-nucleus profiling of 1.1 million hypothalamic nuclei in AD-BXD mice reveals sex-biased, cell-type-specific amyloid responses associated with early non-cognitive features. What is new is the temporal and sex-resolved framing of these glial responses. A separate study links diet-induced obesity to sex-dependent microvascular changes, with capillary loss and cognitive decline in males.

ranked.headline: Memory-efficient algorithms cut runtime and RAM in core sequence analysis tasks
ranked.summary: Five preprints posted 24–26 November 2026 report memory-efficient tools for assembly, alignment, placement and RNA search.
ranked.synthesis: The five preprints share a focus on reducing memory footprint and computation time in sequence analysis at scale. Lash implements UltraLogLog, ExaLogLog and HyperMinHash sketches, reportedly 28–43% more memory-efficient than HyperLogLog for approximating microbial genome content. Gallifrey applies locally consistent de Bruijn graphs to fast PacBio HiFi draft assembly, reportedly more than six times faster than rust-mdbg with half the memory. Local wavefront alignment (lWFA) and bidirectional lBiWFA target exact local alignment while retaining O(sN) time and lowering memory use. gPlace is presented as a memory-bounded drop-in replacement for pplacer that yields identical placements. RNAhub2 adds prefiltering, parallelized searches and NAF compression to structure-based RNA homology searching. The common novelty is algorithmic: bounded or reduced resource use with reported preservation of exactness or compatibility with established tools.

ranked.headline: Transcriptional and epigenetic control of hormone and stress gene expression in plants
ranked.summary: Recent Arabidopsis and rose studies resolve hormone-gene regulation to specific promoters, chromatin marks and splice events.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is regulation of hormone signalling at defined molecular targets, with abscisic acid (ABA) the most frequent node. In rose, RhWUS1 directly represses RhNCED3, reducing ABA biosynthesis, and is itself regulated by cytokinin and auxin factors that control axillary bud outgrowth. In Arabidopsis, SRPKII kinases modulate HAB1 alternative splicing through SR45 phosphorylation, shaping ABA sensitivity during seedling establishment. Other entries extend this framework to chromatin and stress: RSI1/FLD removes H3K4me2/3 at its own transcription start site to limit pathogen-induced expression, and an RHD6-directed network sustains root hair growth under combined low phosphate and salt stress. What is new is resolution to specific promoters, epigenetic marks and splice events.

ranked.headline: Transcription factors and ecdysone oxidase shape lifespan and neuron identity
ranked.summary: Recent preprints link single transcription factors and metabolic genes to neuronal identity, aging, and reproduction in invertebrate models.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is genetic control of cell identity and organismal physiology through transcriptional regulators and metabolic genes. In the Drosophila lamina, the transcription factor dFezf is reported to establish cell-type-specific sets of ion channels and receptors that distinguish L3 luminance from L2 contrast neurons. Two preprints link transcriptional and metabolic regulation to lifespan: loss of C. elegans HLH-30/TFEB alters the basal transcriptome in stage- and age-dependent ways and reduces progeny and larval survival, while disruption of the Drosophila ecdysone oxidase gene fezzik changes transcription, L-dopa levels and sex-specific lifespan, with chinmo implicated in females. A published single-cell study in Saccoglossus kowalevskii adds an evolutionary frame, showing that neuronal cell types diverge widely across animal phyla around a shared core of neuronal genes.

ranked.headline: Mechanical and matrix cues shape vascular and tissue integrity across development
ranked.summary: Recent preprints link contractility, compression, hemodynamics and ECM cues to vascular and lymphatic phenotypes in mice and zebrafish.
ranked.synthesis: The five preprints converge on mechanical and matrix-related cues as determinants of vascular and tissue phenotype, although they differ in system and scope. In aging mouse collecting lymphatics, loss of SRF-driven smooth muscle contractility, rather than smooth muscle cell loss, is associated with vessel dilation and reduced lymph drainage. Extraluminal compression disrupts lymphatic endothelial barrier integrity and promotes inflammation through a Piezo1-CaMKII Ca2+ signaling axis. In zebrafish, klf2a/klf2b, hemodynamic forces and Yap1/Wwtr1-dependent epithelial-endothelial Vegfab-Vegfr2 signaling establish fenestrated endothelial identity in the choroid plexus. Two mouse developmental studies address matrix: Tmem2 loss in the neural crest lineage causes cleft palate with HA accumulation, hypoxia and vascular defects, and Ilk deletion in renal stroma disrupts fibronectin expression and tissue integrity within a defined window. What is new is the emphasis on contractility loss in aging lymphatics and on compression-triggered endothelial dysfunction, alongside developmental roles for ECM regulators.

ranked.headline: Localised auxin perception and expansin delivery control root and petal patterning
ranked.summary: Recent preprints resolve where auxin perception, expansin delivery and vascular patterning are spatially restricted in roots and petals.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is spatial restriction of developmental signals in roots. A synthetic auxin-perception system in defined Arabidopsis root domains shows that outer elongating cells control root growth, and shifting the domain moves the proliferation zone. ROP activation recruits the trichoblast-specific expansin EXPA7 to root hair initiation sites via brefeldin-A-sensitive vesicle trafficking. Metaxylem number is remodelled along wheat and grass root axes, with spatial transcriptomics and hydraulic modelling linking vessel patterning to water transport. An Arabidopsis study on nuclear and chromatin geometry cautions against direct interpretation of CYCB1;1 reporter intensity. In Hibiscus trionum petals, auxin does not initiate bullseye boundaries but preserves their proportions through distal cell behaviour. What is new is the separation of initiation from proportion and expansion, with the petal case being the only non-root example.

ranked.headline: Low-input and archival DNA extend molecular species identification and genomics
ranked.summary: Nanopore and amplification workflows now recover species identities and genomes from century-old, museum and single-larva material.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is molecular inference of species identity, diversity and genomic features from limited or archival material. Nanopore sequencing underlies a barcoding survey of 3,657 European Ulva samples from 30 countries, identifying 46 species and flagging non-indigenous taxa, and a mini-barcoding workflow that recovered COI sequences from 284 of 288 century-old spider museum specimens, adding 53 new BINs to BOLD. Multiple displacement amplification enables WGS and GBS genotyping of single zebra mussel veliger larvae from about 1 ng DNA. Off-target sequencing of 312 spruce bark beetles reveals frequent nematode associates across Europe. The Bermuda skink study instead reports a Nanopore-based annotated reference genome for a Critically Endangered species. What is new is the application of these approaches to low-input and century-old material.

ranked.headline: Cross-layer omics link glycan remodelling to tumor regulatory states
ranked.summary: Matched serum proteomics and N-glycoproteomics, plus glycan–phosphorylation co-variation across 1,211 tumor proteomes, make cross-layer tumor states testable.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints is the integration of multiple molecular layers to resolve tumor regulatory states. Matched serum proteomics and intact N-glycoproteomics from 100 participants, analysed with a new differential-trend-subtype (DTS) framework, link glycan remodelling to ovarian cancer. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, spatial transcriptomics of CA19-9-positive regions yields four transcriptional programs associated with patient survival and cell-line drug sensitivity. PTMlink extends this logic to post-translational regulation by scoring glycosylation–phosphorylation co-variation across 1,211 tumor proteomes. What is new is the testability of cross-layer relationships, in which co-variation and molecular signatures are quantified directly rather than inferred from single modalities. The remaining items, a machine learning analysis of long COVID transcriptomes and an integrated breast and ovarian gene-expression screen, apply similar integrative logic in more exploratory, hypothesis-generating settings.

ranked.headline: Perturbations alter barrier and neural cell populations in mouse and iPSC models
ranked.summary: Preprints and one published study link neonatal, genetic and maternal exposures to cell-specific neurovascular and neural changes.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is cell-resolved readout of neural and neurovascular compartments following a defined perturbation or genetic risk variant. Neonatal SARS-CoV-2 spike protein exposure in mice produced region-specific changes in SOX2-positive cells and TBR1 neurons at P10, without broad cerebrovascular or BBB alterations. In iPSC-derived models, the NOTCH3 p.R544C CADASIL variant was associated with early BBB failure, complement-matrix activation and metabolic dysregulation, while blood-brain barrier cells from 22q11.2 deletion carriers showed structural and metabolic differences linked to schizophrenia penetrance. The published study reports that maternal TPOAb positivity in mice was associated with placental inflammation, fetal BBB disruption, hippocampal microglial activation and altered BDNF/synaptic signaling. What is new is the focus on specific barrier and neural cell populations, including progenitors, neurons and microglia, across rodent and human-derived systems. Most evidence remains preprint-stage and associative.

ranked.headline: Distinct sensors and extraction routes drive organelle stress remodeling
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and one JCB report assign specific sensors, tethers and extraction factors to organelle stress responses.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that stressed organelles are remodeled through defined protein-level routes rather than a single shared mechanism. In the OXA1L study, copper binding disrupts mitoribosome assembly and releases MRPL20 to the nucleus, where ATF5-driven UPRmt restrains cuproptosis. The ATAD1 study places ATAD1 at mitochondria-ER contact sites in HeLa cells, where it moves mislocalized Pex26 from mitochondria to the ER. A VCP-dependent pathway degrades ER membrane proteins after induced ubiquitination, bypassing canonical ERAD. A dynamic pSILAC knockdown screen of HECT E3 ligases adds a systems view, reporting UPS-wide redundancy, compensation between E3s, and substrates affecting MCL1 turnover. What is new is the assignment of a specific sensor, tether or extraction factor to each context. These items do not establish a shared mechanism across all organelles.

ranked.headline: Stressors and contextual modifiers reshape aquatic organism physiology and behaviour
ranked.summary: Life stage, food availability, habitat and chemical exposure each alter how aquatic animals respond to stressors, according to four recent studies.
ranked.synthesis: The four items examine how stressors alter performance in aquatic animals, with responses depending on context rather than being fixed. In the Oikopleura dioica preprint, anthropogenic noise changes behaviour in a life stage- and signal-specific way, with larvae appearing most sensitive. A meta-analysis of freshwater invertebrates and fish, also a preprint, reports that sublethal chemical exposure lowers heat tolerance and increases its variability. In the published study of the leather star Dermasterias imbricata, food availability modifies immune, behavioural, metabolic and survival responses to prolonged thermal stress. In published work on cyprinid fish, hypoxia tolerance and oxygen supply capacity differ between lentic and lotic species. The new element is explicit treatment of contextual modifiers, including life stage, nutritional state and habitat, as determinants of stress responses. The Oikopleura and meta-analysis findings remain provisional, and sound-specific evidence is limited to the Oikopleura preprint.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks question whether variant and perturbation predictors recover causal effects
ranked.summary: Foundation models and virtual knock-out tools are now tested against ClinVar, DepMap and single-cell data, exposing limits of current benchmarks.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how well predictive models of genetic and transcriptional effects can be evaluated and trusted. Zero-shot virtual knock-out tools (scTenifoldKnk, CellOracle, Geneformer) tested on single-cell and DepMap data produce rankings that mostly reflect network topology rather than causal genes. In variant interpretation, six genomic foundation models benchmarked on 6,960 ClinVar variants in LGMD genes favor Evo2 with 501 bp context, although clinical utility remains untested. A Manski-bounds analysis shows that many pairwise comparisons of variant effect predictors are undecided because of unscored variants, motivating reach-aware reporting. SpliceVarMech adds a causal generative, Bayesian framework aimed at mechanistic interpretation of non-canonical splicing variants, benchmarked on male infertility genes and BRCA1. What is new is the emphasis on causal validity and variant coverage, rather than headline accuracy alone.

ranked.headline: New methods infer relatedness, mixtures and ancient gene duplications
ranked.summary: Four preprints introduce scalable inference tools for ancient DNA relatedness, hominin mtDNA mixtures, and deep eukaryote phylogeny.
ranked.synthesis: The four preprints share a methodological focus: computational frameworks that extract evolutionary relationships from historical or deep-time genomic data. Fastpmr provides a fast, memory-efficient pairwise mismatch-rate method for biological relatedness inference across the Allen Ancient DNA Resource. TrailMix estimates mixture proportions and phylogenetic placement of hominin mtDNA lineages in ancient samples, using a pangenomic reference graph. Two further studies address deep phylogeny and gene family evolution. One uses 219 pre-LECA ancient gene duplication families and phylogenetic reconciliation to test candidate root positions of the eukaryote tree. H2O combines Ks distributions, tree-based duplication calls and paralogy-aware filtering to improve detection of large-scale gene family expansions. What is new is the application of these inferences to large archives and the explicit handling of mixture, paralogy and duplication evidence.

ranked.headline: Cryo-EM and FIB workflows resolve cellular ultrastructure with targeted precision
ranked.summary: Cryo-ET, fluorescence-guided FIB milling and ptychographic cryo-EM now combine large-area, targeted and near-atomic readouts in cells and parasite samples.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is automation of electron microscopy workflows that make nanoscale ultrastructure both targetable and quantifiable. A stitched 3D cryo-electron tomography montage reveals heterogeneous yet connected Arp2/3 branched actin networks across lamellipodia of migrating cells. Fluorescence-guided 3D FIB milling is introduced for locating rare structures in high-pressure-frozen samples, validated by recovery of centrosomes. Ptychographic single-particle cryo-EM adds automated probe estimation and dose-fractionation, reaching 3.3 Å resolution. Deep-learning-assisted FIB-SEM reconstructs Plasmodium falciparum oocyst ultrastructure and segments sporozoites synchronously. What is new is the combination of fluorescence-guided targeting, automated parameter estimation and deep-learning segmentation for volumetric imaging of rare structures. All four items are preprints, so the evidence remains unreviewed.

ranked.headline: Structural and regulatory mechanisms of ATP-driven AAA+ and SecA machines
ranked.summary: Four preprints report how autoinhibition, aptamer binding, partial cooperativity and pseudo-helicase motifs govern AAA+ and translocation machinery.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is conformational control of energy-coupled molecular machines, in which ATP binding and hydrolysis, subunit coordination or regulatory domain switching determine function. In the archaeal VAT heterohexamer, reconstituted with motif-dependent partial cooperativity, ATP hydrolysis and substrate unfolding respond differently, indicating that these outputs are not obligately linked. The SecA study places pseudo-helicase motifs in ATP-driven coupling to polypeptide translocation through the SecYEG channel, tested by site-directed mutagenesis. The p97 study shows that a DNA aptamer binding the dynamic p47 adaptor remodels its regulatory architecture through allosteric binding and serves as a chemical biology probe. The TsaP crystal structure reveals autoinhibition of its LysM domain, which PilQ binding relieves to anchor type IV pilus secretins to peptidoglycan. Together, these preprints extend mechanistic detail on how regulatory states gate activity across bacterial, archaeal and p97-family systems.

ranked.headline: Brain Network Connectivity Tracks Cognitive Control and Reward Sensitivity
ranked.summary: Repeated and two-year fMRI designs now test whether network connectivity and vascular markers reliably track effort, control, and reward-related behavior.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these four preprints is the relationship between measured brain network properties and individual differences in effort, cognitive control, and value-based behavior. One study tests whether effort-related behavior and nucleus accumbens resting connectivity show psychometric reliability across repeated sessions in 84 adults. Another relates regional arterial elasticity in cortical networks, estimated with pulse-DOT PReFx, to cognitive control costs during task switching across brain networks. A third shows that working-memory load in a dynamic bandit task reduces directed exploration and reconfigures aIns-IPS coupling within an fMRI decision network. A two-year longitudinal fMRI study of 332 emerging adults links rising ventral attention network connectivity to reward and punishment sensitivity, with self-control decline as the mediating pathway. The new element is the emphasis on longitudinal and repeated-measure designs, paired with network-level readouts of vascular and connectivity markers tied to behavior.

ranked.headline: Genomic and eDNA tools resolve polar algal reproduction and marine community shifts
ranked.summary: Four preprints apply single-cell genetics, eDNA, in vitro and metagenomic approaches to snow algae, diatoms, corals and plankton.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of molecular and genomic data to infer ecological traits of marine and polar organisms. Single-cell population genetics of Chlainomonas sp. blooms indicates a haploid-diploid life cycle with clonal reproduction and likely high selfing. In two Southern Ocean diatoms, in vitro work distinguishes proton-pumping rhodopsin light-harvesting strategies under varying iron and light spectra. Seawater eDNA metabarcoding at Mermaid Reef tracks coral community restructuring after a 2025 heatwave and matches photo-transect cover and assemblage patterns. A comparison of global open-ocean plankton diversity across occurrence, abundance, biomass and metagenomic data reports a latitudinal gradient. What is new is the explicit cross-checking of molecular readouts against conventional census methods, most clearly in the coral and plankton studies.

ranked.headline: Structural analyses probe disease variants, microproteins and prion-like domains
ranked.summary: Four preprints apply structural and disorder analyses to human variants, fusion proteins, microproteins and retroelement prion-like domains.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of structural and sequence-level features to infer protein behaviour where direct experimental characterization is limited. For disease-linked CTSC missense variants in Papillon-Lefevre syndrome, predicted protein destabilization is linked to ClinVar pathogenicity labels. Testing four protein-folding tools on control, cancer-associated and fusion proteins shows that inter-tool agreement does not establish biological plausibility, a caution against treating prediction consensus as evidence. Structural and biophysical analysis of 30 human de novo microproteins reports intrinsic disorder and short linear motifs. In an evolutionary analysis, 26 prion-like domains were identified among 2,636 mobile element proteins, all within LTR retroelement Gag proteins, and phylogenetic mapping suggests an ancestral origin. The new element is the restriction of these prion-like domains to LTR retroelement Gag proteins, which links sequence-level screening to lineage history.

ranked.headline: Accelerated and quantum methods for haplotype phasing and somatic variant calling
ranked.summary: Preprints report GPU, quantum and reproducibility-focused implementations of haplotype and variant inference on sequencing and single-cell atlas data.
ranked.synthesis: The four preprints share a computational focus on inferring genomic state from sequencing or single-cell data rather than a common reference framework. Phirefly performs hierarchical read-based haplotype phasing at chromosome scale, with key steps run on quantum hardware and accuracy reported as comparable to QHap and mainstream approaches. BRISANCE applies a GPU-accelerated Parabricks pipeline to somatic short-variant detection in HG008 tumor-normal WGS, reporting 73.66% overlap with DRAGEN and a 20.6-fold runtime improvement. CyteArc analyzes remote single-cell atlases in place at about 100 million cells, with provenance tracking. The Fusion transpiler study tests whether SNHA network-inference code remains functionally identical across nine languages. What is new is the emphasis on implementation: hardware acceleration, scale and cross-language reproducibility are evaluated alongside inference accuracy.

ranked.headline: Prior signaling and macrophage lineage calibrate innate antiviral and cytokine responses
ranked.summary: Four 2026 preprints show that cytokine history, cell lineage, and viral proteins shape innate immune output in macrophages and microglia-like cells.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread across these preprints is that prior state and cell identity calibrate innate immune output rather than acute stimulation alone. In primary human macrophages, earlier cytokine exposure constrains later transcriptional responses, with IFNβ dominating. Syngeneic iPSC-derived microglia-like and CAM-like macrophages show distinct TLR-driven NF-κB responses, differing HIV permissiveness, and varied cART responses, indicating lineage-dependent behavior. In microglia-like cells, Zika virus NS2B suppresses the PA28 immunoproteasome during the innate antiviral response. A modeling study links cytokine feedback to strain-specific immune responses to avian coronavirus. What is new is the explicit dependence of these responses on signaling history and macrophage lineage, with viral proteins and feedback loops acting as modifiers of that calibration. The avian coronavirus and Zika items are less direct tests of the macrophage history and lineage question than the two macrophage studies.
